name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: MCP Server Maven Plugin is a Java 17 Maven plugin that starts a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) HTTP server from a Maven project. Its aggregator goals expose configured Machai AI tools to MCP clients with either stateless HTTP or streamable HTTP transport. Each goal uses the current Maven project's name, version, and base directory; loads a PropertiesConfigurator from the configured properties file; applies additional parameters as JVM system properties without overwriting properties already supplied to the JVM; configures the listening port; registers configured tools; and starts one server for a multi-module reactor. It is intended for repeatable local development, integration tests, demonstrations, and build-driven MCP automation. A lifecycle function tool allows an MCP client to request a delayed, orderly JVM shutdown after work completes.

constructors.description: Creates the Maven Mojo that starts a stateless HTTP MCP server. Maven creates and configures this Mojo when the stateless goal is invoked.

examples.description: Maven instantiates org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStatelessServerMojo for this fully configured stateless-server invocation.

constructors.description: Creates the Maven Mojo that starts a streamable HTTP MCP server. Maven creates and configures this Mojo when the streamable goal is invoked.

examples.description: Maven instantiates org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.HttpStreamableMcpServerMojo for this fully configured streamable-server invocation.

constructors.description: Creates the tool provider that exposes MCP server lifecycle controls, including delayed shutdown.

examples.description: The MCP server configuration registers this tool provider so an MCP client can invoke its lifecycle operation.

features.name: stateless Maven goal
features.description: Runs the aggregator stateless goal. It applies additional parameters, loads the MCP configuration, creates an org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStatelessMcpServer with Maven project metadata, supplies the project directory and HTTP port, registers configured tools, and starts the server. Invalid configuration or startup failures are reported as Maven execution errors.

examples.description: Start a stateless MCP HTTP endpoint for the current Maven project. Install or resolve the plugin by using its fully qualified Maven coordinates, place tool and provider settings in the referenced properties file, then run this command from the project or reactor root.

features.name: streamable Maven goal
features.description: Runs the aggregator streamable goal. It performs the common parameter and configuration setup, creates an org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.HttpStreamableMcpServer, configures the project directory and port, registers configured tools, and starts the streamable HTTP server.

examples.description: Start a streamable HTTP MCP endpoint. First configure the Machai server and tools in the specified properties file, then invoke the streamable goal from the Maven project root for a client that requires this transport.

features.name: applyParameters
features.description: Copies non-null entries from the Mojo parameter map to JVM system properties only when the property is not already set. This preserves explicit JVM property values and permits credentials or provider settings to be supplied through Maven configuration.

examples.description: Supply a runtime property directly on the Maven command line so it takes precedence over a same-named value that could be provided through the plugin parameter map.

features.name: stopMcpServer
features.description: Requests orderly MCP server shutdown. The operation returns an acknowledgement immediately, then performs a delayed shutdown, records final usage statistics, and exits the JVM with the requested exit code. The default exit code is 0.

examples.snippet: Invoke the configured MCP function stop_mcp_server with {"exit_code": 0} after the client has completed its work.
examples.description: Use the MCP client's function invocation mechanism to request a successful, delayed server termination after finishing an integration-test or automation session.

customizations.name: mcp.port
customizations.description: Required Maven property that selects the HTTP listening port for either server transport.

examples.description: Sets the selected MCP server's listening port to 8080.

customizations.name: mcp.config
customizations.description: Maven property for the MCP properties configuration file. Its absolute path is passed to the Machai PropertiesConfigurator loader; the plugin default is mcp.properties.

examples.description: Points the plugin to the configuration file containing MCP server and tool settings.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo
studs.description: Common Maven Mojo boundary for MCP server transports. It provides shared parameter application and PropertiesConfigurator loading while concrete transport Mojos create the selected server.

examples.snippet: public final class ExampleMojo extends org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo { public void execute() throws org.apache.maven.plugin.MojoExecutionException { applyParameters(); } }
examples.description: A transport-specific Mojo can extend the shared base class to reuse parameter handling.

examples.title: Run a stateless MCP server from Maven
steps: Create a Machai MCP properties file, for example C:\work\demo\mcp.properties, with the server and tool settings required by the application.

From the Maven project or multi-module reactor root, resolve and invoke the plugin by its coordinates: mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.2:stateless -Dmcp.port=8080 -Dmcp.config=C:\work\demo\mcp.properties.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the endpoint exposed on port 8080 and invoke the tools configured in the properties file.
When processing is complete, invoke stop_mcp_server with exit_code 0 through the MCP client to request orderly shutdown.
examples.description: This scenario installs or resolves the plugin on demand through Maven, configures it with a properties file and port, runs a stateless HTTP transport, and terminates it cleanly.

examples.title: Configure the plugin in a Maven build for streamable HTTP
steps: Add the displayed plugin declaration to the build plugins section of the project POM and ensure the referenced properties file is readable.
Run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.2:streamable from the project root, or bind the streamable goal to an appropriate Maven execution.
Use an MCP client that supports streamable HTTP to connect and perform the configured tool operations.
Finish the session by invoking stop_mcp_server when the server is no longer needed.
examples.description: This scenario demonstrates dependency-style Maven plugin installation, persistent server configuration, streamable transport startup, client use, and controlled lifecycle completion.
